question: What will WastewaterSCAN's national norovirus (GII) level category be on October 15, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Latest WastewaterSCAN monthly report (Sept 2026 update, published Oct 2 2026) shows national norovirus GII LOW with no 21-day trend. Last year's analog: LOW on Oct 6 2025, MEDIUM by the Nov 3 2025 report, HIGH by late Nov; the seasonal rise typically starts in early October. Categories use national tertiles of the trailing 365 days. The 2025-26 season stayed HIGH into late May 2026, so the lower tertile is roughly the Jun-Sep 2026 lull, and a modest seasonal uptick tips it to Medium. Question background says some early-October reporting showed Medium (unverified). The window is about 10 days of data, and the last confirmed reading is Low with no trend, so this leans only slightly to Medium. High needs an unusually fast surge. No market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or with bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- WWSCAN Sept 2026 update (published 2026-10-02): national norovirus GII LOW, low concentrations, no trend in last 21 days, detected in 99% of Sept samples.
- WWSCAN Aug 2026 update (early Sept 2026; MedicalDaily 2026-09-21): national LOW, no trend; Aug median concentrations down ~12% from July. CDC NoroSTAT: 27 outbreaks Aug 1-Sep 4, within normal range.
- NBC (2026-05-29): national still HIGH in late May 2026 (2025-26 season long and elevated; GII.17 plus GII.4 circulating).
- 2025 analog: Sept 2025 update (pub 2025-10-06) LOW, no trend, sites 88 low/31 med/15 high; Sept median up 16% vs Aug. Oct 2025 update (pub 2025-11-03) MEDIUM, no trend, sites 72 low/44 med/19 high; South rising from mid-Sept 2025. Late Nov 2025: HIGH, concentrations up 69% since October.
- 2024-25 season: rise began early October, peak early February (WWSCAN).
- Category method: combines 21-day trend, national tertiles of the past 365 days, and detection frequency. The trailing 365 days currently include the long 2025-26 high season, so the lower tertile is roughly the Jun-Sep 2026 lull.
- Question background claims some early-Oct 2026 reporting said MEDIUM while a dashboard snapshot said LOW; could not locate that report.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the national Norovirus GII category on data.wastewaterscan.org for the latest point on or before 2026-10-15 (observed Oct 15-16), not the monthly blog reports.
- Event window: single reading dated on or before 2026-10-15; as of 2026-10-05 there are about 10 days of data remaining.
- Searched but not found: any live dashboard reading (the JS dashboard would not render), a news article stating national Medium in Oct 2026, and any market (none on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: WastewaterSCAN national norovirus GII category in mid-October over the 2024 and 2025 seasons (Low in early Oct, Medium by early Nov, rise beginning early-to-mid Oct)

calls.reasoning: The latest confirmed reading (Sept 2026 update, published Oct 2) is national LOW with no 21-day trend and a median flat vs August. The 365-day comparison window contains the long, high 2025-26 season, so the low tertile is roughly the Jun-Sep 2026 lull; current levels are at or near the top of that. In 2025, early October was still LOW and MEDIUM came by the Nov 3 report. The 2024 rise began in early October. With about 10 days of data left and a possible lag, the status quo LOW is modestly favored. calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: Sept 2026 LOW, no trend; the 2025 analog was LOW in early Oct and MEDIUM by the Nov 3 update. They differ on (a) how much weight to give the question background's unverified claim of early-October MEDIUM reporting and (b) how fast the seasonal rise usually crosses the tertile boundary. I ran 2 searches aimed at the claimed October 2026 MEDIUM report. Both returned only older WWSCAN updates (Oct 2025 MEDIUM, June 2026 MEDIUM) and a MedicalDaily piece on the August LOW. Neither search found any October 2026 MEDIUM report, so the claim stays unverified. It is still plausible, because the dashboard updates daily and the question author may have seen it. I keep the runs' reference class. I land between Run 3 and Runs 1-2 because the status quo plus the 2025 timing favor LOW, but the claimed near-boundary state makes MEDIUM a real risk.
